A government watchdog report reveals FEMA workers bypassed Trump-supporting homes after Hurricane Milton, breaching federal law and agency policy.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: A report from the Department of Homeland Security’s Office of Inspector General (OIG) has confirmed that Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) workers intentionally skipped homes displaying Trump flagsduring relief efforts following Hurricane Milton in October 2024. The workers cited political signage as justification for bypassing properties, violating the Hatch Act and internal FEMA policies.
📺 DETAIL: The Inspector General’s report, released Monday, verified 11 documented cases of politically motivated discrimination, with one FEMA worker explicitly noting, “did not visit due to Trump flag.”The scandal, initially exposed by a whistleblower, revealed systemic failures in FEMA’s training and oversight. FEMA’s own Office of Professional Responsibility initially downplayed the issue, with the OIG criticizing the agency for inadequate supervision and failure to document survivor interactions properly.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “Federal disaster responses are supposed to serve every American equally, no matter who they voted for or what sign is in their yard,” a DHS official commented.
🎯 IMPACT: The scandal previously led to the firing of FEMA Supervisor Marn’i Washington and three crew members, who were implicated in the politically motivated discrimination. Notably, Washington complained at the time that she was being scapegoated, and that such actions were widespread at the agency. President Donald J. Trump has cited the case in an executive order addressing political bias in FEMA.
📺 FLASHBACK: The allegations first surfaced when internal FEMA messages revealed a supervisor instructed workers to avoid homes with Trump signage. FEMA initially claimed the incident was isolated, but whistleblower accounts and subsequent investigations revealed broader issues.
A new survey has revealed that France’s Marine Le Pen is leading all potential opponents in the 2027 French presidential race, reflecting a growing rightward shift across Europe.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: Marine Le Pen, leader of France’s National Rally (RN) party, is on track to win the 2027 French presidential election,according to a new poll.
📺 DETAIL: According to a survey by Toluna-Harris, a market research firm, Le Pen is projected to win the second roundof the 2027 presidential election against all likely opponents. French presidential elections used a two-round run-off system. In the first round, all candidates from all parties are permitted to stand. If no candidate receives more than 50 percent of the vote, the two most popular candidates progress to the run-off ballot, from which all other candidates and parties are barred. The winner of the run-off ballot becomes President. According to the survey, Le Pen is favored over the far-left Jean-Luc Mélenchon (68 percent versus 32 percent). Le Pen is also favored over so-called centrists Édouard Philippe (55 percent versus 45 percent) and Gabriel Attal (57 percent versus 43 percent). The same survey revealed that, in the first round, Le Pen is projected to secure 35 percent of the vote. In contrast, Mélenchon is on 16 percent, Philippe is on 14 percent, and Attal is on eight percent. Glucksmann, a center-left candidate who supports surrendering much more national sovereignty to the European Union (EU), secured ten percent, while the center-right Retailleau secured six percent, and the eco-socialist Tondelier secured three percent.
🎯 IMPACT: A Le Pen victory would represent the first presidential victory for National Rally in the party’s history. The support for Le Pen demonstrates the shift towards populism across Europe, reflecting support for Giorgia Meloni in Italy and Nigel Farage’s Reform UK party,among other examples. The findings show that while the far-left Mélenchon is Le Pen’s primary rival in the first round, a centrist candidate has a better chance of beating her in the second round.
📺 FLASHBACK: These results reflect similar findings published earlier this year. Back in July, a survey conducted by the French Institute of Public Opinion (IFOP) showed Le Pen beating Attal (54 percentvs 46 percent), Philippe (55 percentvs 45 percent), and Mélenchon (70 percentvs 30 percent) in the second round. The same survey also showed that Le Pen would receive roughly a third of the vote (36 percent). If she faces a centrist candidate in the second round, the survey projected that Le Pen would unite 50 percentof the right-leaning vote. If up against Mélenchon, Le Pen would unite 90 percentof the right-leaning vote.

The governing Labour Party’s ban on new oil and gas exploration licenses and continued windfall taxes are projected to decimate the workforce of Britain’s North Sea oil and gas sector.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: Britain’s North Sea oil and gas sector is set to lose over 100,000 jobs,according to new data from Britain’s Department for Energy Security and Net Zero.
📺 DETAIL: According to data from the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), Britain’s North Sea oil and gas sector will lose more than 113,000 positionsover the next 25 years. This constitutes an 82.7 percent collapse in the workforce. The collapse stems from the governing Labour Party’s energy policies, such as the ban on new oil and gas exploration licenses and the continuation of windfall taxes. The DESNZ data was acquired by a Freedom of Information request. Specifically, it was revealed that the number of jobs in the sector is on track to decline from 136,675 in 2024 to 23,584 jobs by 2050. In 2026, there are currently 115,720 jobs in the sector. The data revealed that 54,268 jobs would be lost by 2030, and over half of the jobs in the sector would vanish by 2035. According to the DESNZ, every role in the industry sustains an additional 4.4 jobsin the wider supply chain.
🎯 IMPACT: This represents another blow to the North Sea oil and gas sector. The month prior, British Petroleum (BP) announced plans to sell off its North Sea assets due to the British government’s climate policies. “Unless investors have confidence that Britain is open for business, more capital, more jobs and more expertise will continue to leave,” warned Russell Borthwick, Chief Executive of the Aberdeen & Grampian Chamber of Commerce, back in July. This data is likely to strain Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s relationship with President Donald J. Trump, who has repeatedly urged the British government to restart drilling in the North Sea. “You have one of the most valuable oil finds anywhere in the world, and if the United Kingdom would use it, they’d be a wealthy country again… I could not get Starmer to use it. It was incredible,” he told the press earlier this month. The projections coincide with mounting pressure on the Prime Minister, who has already delayed a decision on approving new oil and gas projects in the North Sea to appease green ideologues in his party. Specifically, the government is weighing up the approval of the Rosebank and Jackdaw projects. Proponents argue that they could safeguard 3,500 jobsand generate over £20 billion (~$27 billion)in economic benefits.
📺 FLASHBACK: Upon entering office back in July, Prime Minister Burnham appointed Miatta Fahnbulleh,a Liberia-born Net Zero hardliner,as his Secretary for Energy Security and Net Zero. Raheem Kassam, Editor-in-Chief of The National Pulse, noted in July that “Much like Rep. Ilhan Omar in America, Miatta’s family actually worked for the government they later fled… Her grandfather was evencharged with treason for cavorting with Chinese communistsin the late 1960s. Miatta is just another in a long line of anti-Western, far leftists.”

Consumer confidence in the U.S. has hit a seven-month low, driven by high gas prices and ongoing economic uncertainty linked to inflation and geopolitical tensions.
PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED: Americans’ confidence in the economy declined again in August as high gasoline prices, inflation, and concerns over the conflict in Iran weighed on consumers. The Conference Board said Tuesday that its consumer confidence index fell to 89.4 from 90.2 in July, marking its lowest level in seven months. Survey responses collected between August 3 and August 16 showed increased concerns about prices, gasoline, food, trade, jobs, and geopolitical tensions
📺 DETAIL: Inflation remains a major frustration, with the personal consumption expenditures price index rising 3.7 percent in June from a year earlier, compared with 2.5 percent when President Donald J. Trump took office in January 2025. Views of the current labor market improved slightly, with 27 percent of respondents saying jobs were plentiful, up from 24.4 percent in July. However, expectations for the labor market weakened, with only 14.6 percent expecting more jobs to become available over the next six months.
🎯 IMPACT: The decline in consumer confidence highlights growing concerns about inflation, gasoline prices, and a possibly weakening labor market, which could put additional pressure on the Trump administration to refocus on the economy. With the midterm elections approaching, continued frustration over household costs and employment could become a significant political liability for Republicans.
📺 FLASHBACK: Consumer confidence readings were consistently above 100 in late 2024 and early 2025, before inflationary pressures and geopolitical tensions began to take their toll. Gas prices and inflation have become key issues since the Iran war started earlier this year, resulting in the Strait of Hormuz, which carries much of the world’s energy supplies, being choked off by Iranian forces.

President Trump has suggested renaming Lake Ontario to “Lake America” as U.S.-Canada trade tensions escalate following failed negotiations and new tariffs.

❓ WHAT HAPPENED:PresidentDonald J. Trumpescalated his dispute with Canada on Tuesday by suggesting the United States could rename Lake Ontario “Lake America.” This follows Ontario Premier Doug Ford branding Trump a “dictator” and threatening to cut off Ontarian electricity supplies to the U.S. Trump also accused Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney of falsely claiming that Washington sought changes to protections for the French language in Canada, saying he would never interfere with Canadians speaking French and accusing Carney of using the issue to gain political support in French-speaking Quebec.
📺 DETAIL: The latest clash follows the collapse of trade negotiations last week, which triggered new tariffsand threats of retaliation between the two countries. Vice President JD Vance defended the Trump administration’s position Monday, accusing Canada of treating Chinese goods more favorably than American products and blaming Ottawa for making unreasonable demands during negotiations. Trump has announced 50 percent tariffs on Canadian automobiles, auto parts, trucks, and steelbeginning January 1, 2027. Ontario, Canada’s most populous province, is a major part of the integrated U.S.-Canadian auto industry, while Lake Ontario borders both Ontario and New York. Despite the escalating rhetoric, Vance said the United States remains willing to negotiate and expects Canada to agree to fair trade terms.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “The United States is giving serious consideration to changing the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America in that we don’t expect to [be] doing much business with Ontario any longer.” – President Trump
🎯 IMPACT: The escalating dispute could further strain U.S.-Canada economic relations and increase costs for industries that depend on cross-border trade, particularly the auto sector.

Newcastle-under-Lyme Borough Council, led by Nigel Farage’s Reform UK party, scrapped net zero targets, saving taxpayers over £10.5 million.

❓ WHAT HAPPENED: Newcastle-under-Lyme Borough Council, under the leadership of Nigel Farage’s Reform UK party, has canceled the green agenda targets it inherited to reachnet zero carbon emissions by 2030, resulting in taxpayer savings exceeding £10.5 million (~$14.3m).
📰 DETAIL: The council’s decision reversed a 2019 declaration of a supposed “climate emergency” and halted planned expenditures on expensive net zero initiatives, including £2.191 million (~$3m) for electric refuse vehicles and £4.2 million (~$5.7m) for charging infrastructure. Additional savings were identified in other net zero projects.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “We have pulled the plug on the previous administration’s Net Zero spending spree and put taxpayers first. No family would rip out a perfectly good boiler in their own home when it still works, and the council should have the same common sense mentality. Every pound belongs to the taxpayer. PULSE POINTS
❓ WHAT HAPPENED:Iowa has asked the U.S. Supreme Court to review a ruling blocking a state law that makes certain illegalimmigration offenses a crime under state law. Senate File 2340, passed in April 2024, applies to people who have previously been deported or denied entry into the United States.
📺 DETAIL: The law was quickly challenged by pro-illegal immigrant advocacy groups, and the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals upheld a lower court injunction preventing its enforcement in October 2025. Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird subsequently sought review by the full appeals court, but that request was rejected, leading the state to seek Supreme Court intervention. The formerBiden regime had separately sued to block the law, but the Justice Department dropped its case after President Donald J. Trump took office. Iowa argues that the measure does not create a separate immigration system, but instead supports federal enforcement policy. The Federation for American Immigration Reform (FAIR) has filed a brief supporting Iowa, arguing that states can pass laws that assist federal immigration enforcement without conflicting with federal authority.
💬 KEY QUOTE: “States have always had the right to defend themselves… by passing laws that assist the federal government in enforcing immigration laws.” – Christopher J. Hajec, deputy general counsel, FAIR
🎯 IMPACT: The case could have major implications for state-level immigration enforcement. A Supreme Court ruling in Iowa’s favor could give states broader authority to prosecute certain immigration violations, while a ruling against Iowa would force pro-border state governments to rely on Washington to manage immigration policy responsibly, which did not happen under Biden.

sources.news_title: Report Finds FEMA Deliberately Skipped Homes With Trump Signs
sources.text:
FEMA relief workers who intentionally passed over homes displaying support for Donald Trump after Hurricane Milton violated both federal law and agency rules, according to a sharply critical government watchdog report obtained by Our News Outlet.
The findings, released Monday by the Department of Homeland Security’s Office of Inspector General, substantiate allegations that some disaster response workers made politically motivated decisions in the weeks before the 2024 presidential election. The report also shows that employees cited “Trump flag” in official records as the reason for skipping hurricane victims.
The extraordinary review, based on an internal audit of FEMA’s response to the October 2024 hurricane, confirms a key claim made by a whistleblower who brought the scandal to light shortly after Trump’s 2024 election victory. It also points to serious breakdowns within the federal agency tasked with delivering disaster aid to Americans in crisis.
The report’s headline was unequivocal: “FEMA Disaster Response Crew Violated Law and Policy by Skipping Homes with Political Signage.”
Using surveys filed by crew members at the time, investigators confirmed 11 cases in late October 2024 in which disaster workers bypassed properties for improper reasons. In one entry cited in the report, a worker wrote that the team “did not visit due to Trump flag.”
That figure may account for only a small share of the homes that were actually missed, an insider told Our News Outlet, noting that most of the related notes were left blank.
A source told Our News Outlet that the crew members’ conduct breached FEMA policy and the Hatch Act, the federal law restricting political activity by government employees. Violations can result in civil penalties, including termination, fines and forfeiture of pay.
“This is unacceptable for any public servant,” a DHS official said. “Federal disaster responses are supposed to serve every American equally, no matter who they voted for or what sign is in their yard.”
Charlotte County workers clear feet of sand from a road on southern Manasota Key, in Florida, following the passage of Hurricane Milton in October 2024
A bombshell report released Monday shows Office of Inspector General found FEMA relief crews’ politically charged actions after Hurricane Milton violated federal law as well as agency policy
‘These actions crossed a line that should never be tolerated, especially during a disaster when people are at their most vulnerable and counting on their government to show up and help when they need it most.’
The scandal came to light days after the 2024 election, when the Daily Wire reported on internal messages in which a FEMA supervisor told workers to ‘avoid homes advertising Trump’ as they worked around Lake Placid, Florida.
The crew bypassed at least 20 homes due to the guidance passed down by Washington, the publication reported.
FEMA Supervisor Marn’i Washington, who reportedly relayed the message in a group chat and verbally, was later fired along with three crew members.
Republicans in Congress and Florida Governor Ron DeSantis made sweeping claims accusing the Biden administration of deliberately denying disaster aid to Trump supporters.
Upon taking office, Trump cited the case in signing an executive order creating a council to review ‘serious concerns of political bias in FEMA.’
FEMA’s Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR), releasing its own review in March 2025, ‘found no evidence that this was a systemic problem, nor that it was directed by agency or field leadership,’ according to a Politico report at the time.
However, the IG came down hard on officials for failing to properly train and supervise disaster responders, and fully document survivor interactions.
The report shows the watchdog was able to confirm 11 instances in which disaster workers bypassed properties for improper reasons, including one entry that simply stated, ‘did not visit due to Trump flag’, according to the report
A photo emerged showing a list of instructions on the ‘best practices’ for the agency’s successful relief intervention included directives such as ‘not [ sic ] one goes anywhere alone,’ ‘communicate and follow the rules,’ and avoid homes advertising Trump,’ among others
FEMA Supervisor Marn’i Washington, who reportedly relayed the message in a group chat and verbally, was later fired along with three crew members
The watchdog, which recommends an overhaul of the system, said the problems continued under former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem’s leadership.
The Inspector General claimed DHS made their job more difficult by restricting investigators’ access to records and information.
It also faulted leadership for allowing a contract for FEMA’s Field Assessment and Collection Tools to lapse in September 2025, when then Secretary Kristi Noem did not act on FEMA’s request to fund it.
‘We requested access to the data in March 2025, but FEMA delays prevented us from obtaining the data prior to the contractor abruptly shutting down the system,’ the IG states.
The 10-page report found that most DHS crew leaders and members they interviewed ‘demonstrated no clear understanding of the Hatch Act,’ and that ‘FEMA DSA (Disaster Survivor Assistance) training did not cover ethics rules or Hatch Act provisions.’
‘FEMA DSA policies and procedure did not require crews to add details for why they skipped locations,’ the report adds.
The report found that FEMA crews canvassed 744,000 properties for Hurricane Milton and Hurricane Helene, which struck in late September.
‘According to the FEMA Administrator at the time of the hurricanes and an internal FEMA investigation, after Hurricane Milton, a crew leader instructed their team to avoid homes advertising support for then-Presidential candidate Donald Trump.
In early 2025, upon taking office, Trump cited the case in signing an executive order creating a council to review ‘serious concerns of political bias in FEMA’
FEMA officials talk to residents displaced out of their apartment complex during Hurricane Milton, October 11, 2024, in Clearwater, Florida
‘We conducted this audit to determine the extent to which FEMA followed its policies and procedures when canvassing communities impacted by Hurricanes Helene and Milton for the DSA program.’
It wasn’t until October 28 – nine days after the initial entry – that FEMA OPR became aware of the violations, when it received a whistleblower complaint.
‘We reviewed the daily summary reports for the days the crew skipped 11 homes for unallowable reasons and confirmed they did not contain information on skipping homes due to political signage,’ the agency reports.
The workers were part of a DHS team that was supplemented by volunteers from other agencies.
According to The Daily Wire, one of the workers said: ‘I thought we could go help and make a difference. When we got there we were told to discriminate against people.
‘It’s almost unbelievable to think that somebody in the federal government would think that’s okay.’
A White House spokesperson said: ‘Under Biden, FEMA employees violated FEMA policy and the Hatch Act by refusing aid to disaster survivors who displayed political signs supporting President Trump. No Americans should ever be denied disaster aid because of their political beliefs.’
At the time, a FEMA spokesperson said: ‘While we believe this is an isolated incident, we have taken measures to remove the employee from their role and are investigating the matter to prevent this from happening ever again.
‘The employee who issued this guidance had no authority and was given no direction to tell teams to avoid these homes and we are reaching out to the people who may have not been reached as a result of this incident.’
The statement continued: ‘This is a matter that we take extremely seriously and we are doing everything we can to make sure all survivors receive support from FEMA.
‘We are horrified that this took place and therefore have taken extreme actions to correct this situation and have ensured that the matter was addressed at all levels.’
